Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back with India's response with the bat. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Tammy Beaumont leads her women out as the English players spread out to their respective fielding positions. Smriti Mandhana and Shafali Verma are the two Indian openers. The experienced Lauren Bell to get the chase underway with the ball. Smriti to face. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, in a do-or-die match for the hosts, they will have to bowl their skins out to stop India from claiming the series. Sure, it's an uphill task, but it is doable. We have seen the ball holding up on the pitch and that's where the likes of Sophie Ecclestone and Charlie Dean might come into play. However, with the consistent Indian top order, they will need to pick up early wickets and of course, a win will be guaranteed with all ten wickets taken. Back in a bit for the chase. Stay tuned.

The Indians used spin to full effect, and the bowlers kept the stumps in play, not offering anything to free the arms. The pacers, too, employed those slower ones to make optimal use of the pitch, which kept the batters tied up. In that 7-15 overs phase, England only scored 56 runs while losing three wickets. Overall, the batters did get starts but couldn't hang in there till the end. Sophie Ecclestone and Issy Wong at last provided the finishing touches and helped England to get above a run-a-ball and something for the bowlers to fight for.

England were not express by any means, and the batters struggled to find the right timing. However, they found a stable partnership between Alice Capsey and skipper Tammy Beaumont. The two worked hard to steer England out of trouble. The Indians, on the other hand, continued to be sharp in the field. Just when the partnership was blossoming into something meaningful, and as one brings two, England slipped further down from 68/2 to 70/4, losing Beaumont and Capsey in just a few deliveries.

The start for the hosts was far from ideal as the opening woes for England resurfaced. The pitch was on the slower side and the ball was holding up a bit on the deck as well and Harmanpreet Kaur was quick to spot that and deployed the spin trio. Shree Charani provided the first breakthrough and continued her dream run in the series. England, in an attempt to make the most of the Powerplay, lost both their openers and crawled their way to 38/2.

A late flourish for England in the last over, but still, in all fairness, way below par on the board. A job well done by the Indians with the ball as they used the conditions perfectly to keep the batters at bay. Just four overs went above the single digits for the hosts, and that pretty much sums up their day with the bat, in a must-win match.

SIX! How is that for a finish? A long hop from Deepti, over leg stump, Issy Wong goes deep in the crease, makes room and muscles the pull in front of deep square leg for a six. 16 runs off the over and England Women finish with 126/7 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. It has been a decent bowling display from the Indians on a slowish deck. But after losing both their openers inside the Powerplay itself, England have gathered some momentum since the last few overs as Tammy Beaumont and Alice Capsey have worked hard to steady the ship. With a long tail to follow, this partnership is very crucial from England's point of view and one of these two will have to bat deep to keep England steady.

OUT! CAUGHT! Nicely pouched by Radha Yadav and England Women have lost both openers inside the Powerplay. Deepti Sharma is clever enough to toss the ball up but drag the length back, slow it up and push it wider of the off stump. Sophia Dunkley likes to use her feet and she advances but doesn't reach the pitch of the ball and ends up slicing it in front of point. Yadav moves to her right and scampers across to take it with both hands. Sophia Dunkley departs on 22 (19) and England Women are now 33/2.

OUT! IN THE AIR AND TAKEN! CAUGHT! The dream run for Shree Charani in this series continues as she provides the first breakthrough for India. Loops the ball above the eye level of the batter, full and around off. Danni Wyatt-Hodge's eyes get light up as she gets low on her knee to slog it over the leg side, but loses her shape as she is a bit early into the shot. Goes through and slices it off the toe end of the bat. The ball goes only as far as the mid on region where Arundhati Reddy moves a few yards to her right, and takes a safe catch. Danni Wyatt-Hodge departs for 5 (7) and England are 21/1.

England Women (Playing XI) - Sophia Dunkley, Danni Wyatt-Hodge, Alice Capsey, Paige Scholfield, Amy Jones (WK), Tammy Beaumont (C), Sophie Ecclestone, Issy Wong, Charlie Dean, Lauren Filer, Lauren Bell.
TOSS UPDATE - The flip of the coin lands in favor of England Women they have elected to BAT first.

After a 13-year gap, Old Trafford welcomes back women’s T20I cricket for the first time since England hosted the West Indies in September 2012. As it prepares to stage the fourth game of this series, the ground is set to inscribe another memorable chapter in its illustrious history. Stick around as the toss and team sheets will flash up in a few moments.

India’s openers have laid the perfect platform with two fifty-plus stands, setting up strong starts. The middle order has only come under real pressure once, in the third T20I, and now needs to prove it can rescue the innings whenever those big partnerships break down. Smriti Mandhana has been the standout with over 180 runs and the series’ sole century, while Shree Charani has led the bowling attack, outshining several more established names. With these performances as a springboard, India will be determined to deliver another polished, all-round display in Manchester.

England eventually prevailed in their last outing, but it was anything but comfortable. A sparkling century stand between Sophia Dunkley and Danni Wyatt-Hodge raised hopes, only for the middle order to implode soon after. They leaked runs in the Powerplay and paid the price for a few fielding lapses, yet somehow eked out a win. Their biggest worry now is Natalie Sciver-Brunt being ruled out of the series due to injury, a blow that leaves a massive hole in England’s all-round resources. It is now time for the others to really step up and give their all as a unit.

Every game in this series has been a run-fest packed with fierce competition, injuries notwithstanding. England’s urgency peaked at The Oval, where they dug deep to snatch a close win and keep their hopes alive. India, with an aim to consolidate their lead, are staring at a historic breakthrough. They have never won a T20I series against England, neither at home nor abroad, and this lead is their best shot at finally getting over the line.

Hello, everyone! It’s time for another fresh chapter between England Women and India Women as they gear up to clash in the fourth and the penultimate T20I of this five-match series. From London in the south, the caravan now heads northwards to the historic Old Trafford, Manchester, for this encounter. With the series finely poised at 2-1 in India’s favor, England must win this to force a decider and keep their series hopes alive.
... MATCH DAY ...

The T20I series now heads to the historic Emirates Old Trafford in Manchester, where India Women and England Women will lock horns in the fourth match of this riveting five-game contest. India currently lead the series 2-1, but the momentum has taken a slight tilt after England's spirited comeback win in the third T20I. Each match has been packed with thrill, runs, wickets, and drama, giving fans a brilliant contest between two quality sides. With one more win, India can seal the series, while England will aim to level things and push it into a decider. The stage is set for another gripping battle under the Manchester skies. The third match was a closely fought affair that went right down to the final over. England, batting first, rode on a brilliant opening stand between Sophia Dunkley and Danni Wyatt-Hodge, who stitched together a 137-run partnership. Dunkley’s classy 75 and Danni’s aggressive 66 powered England to a competitive total of 171/9. In reply, India started strong with a flying powerplay and looked in control for the major part, thanks to Smriti Mandhana’s fluent 56 and Shafali Verma’s explosive 47. But the middle order couldn’t quite finish the job, and England held their nerve to clinch a five-run win and stay alive in the series. India Women will be disappointed to have let the previous game slip through their fingers, but there are many positives to take forward. Smriti is in top form, already scoring 181 runs in the series. Shafali and Jemimah have also chipped in with vital runs, while skipper Harmanpreet Kaur’s return to some rhythm is encouraging. The bowling department has found a reliable spinner in Shree Charani, who leads the wicket tally with eight scalps. Deepti and Arundhati have provided breakthroughs as well, but India will want tighter death bowling and a more stable finish in the middle order. There are whispers that Harleen Deol might return in the playing XI for this match, which could boost the batting depth. England Women, meanwhile, will be buoyed by their comeback win, especially in the absence of their regular captain Nat Sciver-Brunt, who has been ruled out of the T20Is due to a groin injury. Tammy Beaumont, standing in as captain, led calmly and used her bowling options smartly. The pace duo of Lauren Filer and Lauren Bell bowled with purpose, while Sophie Ecclestone was again economical and picked up key wickets. Dunkley has been England’s star performer with the bat, and Danni's return to form has added depth. With Sciver-Brunt set to return for the ODIs starting July 16, the rest of the squad will be eager to finish this series strongly and show their potential. As for the conditions in Manchester, the forecast suggests a mostly cloudy day with a chance of a shower or two. While there might be some swing early on due to overhead conditions, Old Trafford is generally a good batting surface. Spinners, too, could come into play as the match progresses. Teams winning the toss might look to chase, keeping in mind the dew and how closely the last game went. Fans can expect another high-quality contest with a lot riding on this one, especially for England, who’ll be fighting to keep the series alive. Who will come out on top? We shall find out soon!
